issuer: the Road Traffic Department (the Controller of Road Traffic)
note: Read 2026-10-30 on the Road Traffic Department's site. The Road Traffic Act (Ch. 220, Statute Law of The Bahamas, the revision the Department publishes, pages of LRO 2002 and 2006), s 34(5): a person under seventeen is disqualified from driving a motor vehicle and shall not be granted any licence to do so (fifteen for an excepted vehicle), so the driver's licence is held from 17 (the learner's permit is from 17 too, with no minimum time on it stated). New Licences: a driver's licence is issued after the theory and practical tests; licences are issued for one or three years and expire at the end of the holder's birth month, but a first licence only for one year, the term held. The first licence's fee is 'calculated at BS$1.66 per month for the duration of the driver's licence'; the months to the end of the birth month aren't fixed, so no total is held and the fee is null (renewals: BS$20 for one year, BS$60 for three, not held as a first issue's). The learner's permit (BS$15) isn't held. No identity card of the Department's is held; transfers of foreign licences weren't read.

sources.title: Road Traffic Act, Ch. 220, Statute Law of The Bahamas, on roadtraffic.gov.bs
sources.said: (5) A person under the age of seventeen years shall be disqualified from driving a motor vehicle and shall not be granted any licence so to do

sources.title: Road Traffic Department, New Licences
sources.said: After successful completion of a theory and practical driving test a driver’s licence is issued. ... Driver’s licences expire at the end of the holder’s birth month and are issued for either one or three years. However, persons obtaining a driver’s licence for the first time can only have their new licence for a period of one year. ... The fees for a first time driver’s licence is calculated at BS$1.66 per month for the duration of the driver’s licence.
